courseReview.name: Personal & Professional Development
courseReview.contribution: develops academic, collaborative and reflective skills for responsible interdisciplinary study

courseReview.name: Research Methods & Statistics
courseReview.contribution: Direct research-methods contribution: operationalisation, experimental design, sampling, inference and a group research project support empirical AI and cognitive-science inquiry.

courseReview.name: AI Ethics
courseReview.contribution: examines fairness, bias, privacy, accountability, human agency and the moral status of AI systems

courseReview.name: Decision-making in AI
courseReview.contribution: covers planning, uncertainty, partial observability and optimisation for intelligent agents

courseReview.name: Logic & Discrete Mathematics
courseReview.contribution: develops logic, discrete structures and mathematical reasoning for computer science and algorithms

courseReview.name: Optimization Methods in AI
courseReview.contribution: develops search, games, constraint satisfaction and optimisation for rational agents

courseReview.name: Reinforcement Learning
courseReview.contribution: Direct AI method: reinforcement-learning frameworks and implemented neural-network agents learn through interaction and trial and error.

courseReview.name: Networks & Operating Systems
courseReview.contribution: develops understanding of network architectures, operating systems, concurrency and resource management

courseReview.name: Database Management Systems
courseReview.contribution: provides relational-database, SQL, normalisation and query-processing foundations

courseReview.name: Software Development
courseReview.contribution: develops software design, testing, maintenance and programming across multiple paradigms

courseReview.name: Algorithms & Data Structures
courseReview.contribution: develops algorithm design, data structures and experimental performance analysis

courseReview.name: Advanced Algorithms
courseReview.contribution: extends algorithmic thinking through algebraic algorithms, mathematical modelling and optimisation

courseReview.name: Introduction to Data Science
courseReview.contribution: develops data cleaning, manipulation, visualisation and an independent applied data project

courseReview.name: Machine Learning
courseReview.contribution: introduces regression, classification, resampling, support-vector machines, trees and clustering

courseReview.name: Image Processing & Computer Vision
courseReview.contribution: develops image processing, feature detection, tracking, object recognition and computer vision

courseReview.name: Neural Networks & Deep Learning
courseReview.contribution: develops neural-network and deep-learning theory and implementation for vision and language applications

courseReview.name: Robotics
courseReview.contribution: develops robotics through kinematics, manipulation, motion planning and collision avoidance

courseReview.name: Introduction to Programming
courseReview.contribution: provides Python programming, debugging, discrete-mathematics and computational problem-solving foundations

courseReview.name: Mathematical Methods
courseReview.contribution: provides calculus, equations and mathematical problem-solving foundations for AI and modelling

courseReview.name: Linear Algebra
courseReview.contribution: provides matrices, vector spaces, eigenvalues and linear transformations used in computational models

courseReview.name: Computational & Numerical Methods
courseReview.contribution: develops numerical algorithms, approximation and computational solutions to mathematical problems

courseReview.name: Linear Systems
courseReview.contribution: Direct mathematical-methods contribution: characterises signals and linear time-invariant systems using convolution, Fourier representations/transforms, Laplace and Z transforms; supplies substantial signal-processing content relevant to the target.

courseReview.name: Probability & Statistics
courseReview.contribution: provides probability theory, distributions, estimation, simulation and statistical inference

courseReview.name: Philosophy of Mind
courseReview.contribution: examines consciousness, the mind-body problem and the possibility of intelligent or conscious machines

courseReview.name: Free Will, Time & the Self
courseReview.contribution: Complementary conceptual inquiry: free will, luck, time and selfhood support critical examination of agency in the target’s philosophical study of intelligence; no AI implementation is claimed.

courseReview.name: Neurobiology
courseReview.contribution: develops neurobiological foundations and experimental understanding of brains and behaviour

courseReview.name: Perception & Action
courseReview.contribution: examines neural mechanisms of sensory processing, perception and goal-directed action

courseReview.name: Higher Order Functions
courseReview.contribution: examines memory, attention, emotion, consciousness, decision-making and cognitive control

courseReview.name: Psycholinguistics
courseReview.contribution: Direct human-language contribution: neurobiological and psychological language production, comprehension, acquisition and impairments; supports cognitive linguistics rather than providing a dedicated computational NLP sequence.

courseReview.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
courseReview.contribution: Direct cognitive foundation: psychological theories, functional brain anatomy, neural communication and behavioural research methods support the target’s cognition/computation relationship.

courseReview.name: Social Psychology
courseReview.contribution: Complementary social-cognition perspective: studies how others influence thoughts, feelings and behaviour; relevant to human interaction with intelligent systems, without claiming an AI-design course.

courseReview.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
courseReview.contribution: develops multivariate statistics and experimental analysis for complex human data

courseReview.name: Advanced Research Seminar
courseReview.contribution: Direct evidence-synthesis method: systematic reviews, meta-analysis, effect sizes and R support evaluation of cognitive and behavioural research; this is not a separate primary-research thesis.

courseReview.name: Lifespan Developmental Psychology
courseReview.contribution: Complementary developmental perspective: cognitive, physical, social and emotional development across the lifespan qualifies how human capacities change; it does not teach computational developmental modelling.
